newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-DESCHAMPS HINTS AT ADIDAS BOYCOTT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DESCHAMPS HINTS AT ADIDAS BOYCOTT.

text.p: France captain Didier Deschamps hinted that his team mates under contract with other sportswear manufacturers may refuse to wear Adidas boots in next month's four-nation tournament in France.
"Let's imagine the 15 players involved all refuse at the same time, excluding themselves from the French team. I wonder what would happen then...," he told sports daily l'Equipe.
The French Soccer Federation has an exclusive contract with Adidas and players must use the company's Adidas boots when playing for France.
When France played Sweden in a friendly last month players under contract with other companies were forced to paint Adidas's famous three stripes on their boots to respect the contract.

"France is one of the last countries in Europe to have a collective contract of this kind," said Deschamps. "The deal will end after the 1998 World Cup. In the meantime, it seems difficult to change things without breaking the rules."
